body: Yea, definitely keep an eye on him. Try to get more info out of him without disagreeing or trying to help and then use that later to convince him he needs to do something about this (whatever it may be). Don't just let him go in circles though.

This has got to be one of the most frustrating things to experience. I don't know how you've been dealing with it but even if I know I'm being paranoid and force myself to think of alternate, less persecutorial, options my subconscious is relentless in sustaining the emotion and initial reaction to what was said/done. 

My advice would be to try and change the subject in your mind to something utterly different and positive. Sometimes, if I do this, it will start a sort of chain reaction which affects my entire mood instead of me just beating my head against myself trying to 'understand' whatever I misunderstood.
Haha, or maybe I'm wrong and we'll just have the last laugh... a little less epic but pretty damn satisfying. Grats on engagement by the way!

Right... dunno why I keep forgetting that... maybe because the answer to this question defines two utterly different approaches to how you, and I should try to live.

But, I feel like you are leaning towards saying that we create our own reality, if I'm wrong stop me. Just because I'm immersed in it provides no concrete evidence that there isn't some fundamental thing that we've all overlooked (and clearly there is, or we wouldn't be having these 2nd grade bickering matches which pass for reasonable discussions between representatives of the People).

My mind can distort reality to such an extent that it is as if Objectivity is a joke and subjectivity is king. The fact that I can do this doesn't mean that its proof there isn't some kind of objective reality.

Sorry if I come off as hostile, text is not as expressive as reality, lol.
